newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Portugal cabinet details conditions of EDP sale.
newsitem.headline: Portugal cabinet details conditions of EDP sale.

text.p: The Portuguese government on Thursday approved a number of conditions for the partial privatisation of state electricity concern EDP, although it left the size of the tranches and the price for a later date.
The sale will comprise an offer to the general public and the sale directly to institutional investors in Portugal and abroad.

The government has said that it plans to privatise between 20 and 30 percent of the company, which is valued at some 1.5 trillion escudos, although it has said the sale could cover as much as 49 percent if there is sufficient demand.

EDP employees will receive a six percent discount on the retail price up to a maximum subscription of 2,000 shares, plus an additional discount of up to five percent, depending on payment options. They will have to hold the shares for three months.
The six percent discount will also be extended to small investors and emigrants for up to 2,000 shares.
There will also be a tranche for EDP bond holders and the general public, with the latter allowed to buy up to 5,000 shares.
Retail investors will receive one bonus share in EDP for every 25 they buy in the offer and hold for one year.
Shares will also be set aside for a greenshoe option.
Pre-registration will run from May 19 to June 6, while the public offer to sell (OPV) will begin on June 9 and close on June 12.
Pricing and allocation is set for June 16 on the Lisbon bourse.
